title: Customer Signal Lens and Actionable Buckets
body:
Purpose:
This note compiles a compact, engineering-actionable view of recent customer feedback across hosted API and Dedicated customers, with an emphasis on Optimize surface-area tradeoffs (batching, caching, quantization recommendations, and rollout controls). Goal is to produce 3 prioritized 'buckets' with proposed probes/experiments and clear owner suggestions so Eng/Product can pick up next week.

Context and constraints:
- Timebox: quick synthesis from Feb 2025 field notes, CS triage board, and telemetry anomalies. Not exhaustive.
- Audience: product-optimize PMs, solutions engineering, runtime and compiler owners.
- Signal sources: CS ticket excerpts, interview notes, cost telemetry (token-per-call delta), and a set of ten customer-provided prompts used in regressions.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Customers are asking for lower-per-token costs without losing deterministic latency and output quality. Three themes rise: 1) smarter defaults for batching + latency SLOs (many customers misconfigure), 2) guardrails and observability for cache effectiveness and KV reuse (hard to see real savings), and 3) simpler quantization guidance that ties to quality expectations per workload. Proposed immediate work: (A) ship a small "batching advisor" UI + API suggestion that recommends safe batch/window sizes by route; (B) add a cache-hit dashboard and conservative cache prewarming probe; (C) publish a short "quantization playbook" and run two A/B probes for opt-level vs. quality on a sample of customers.

Synthesized customer quotes (verbatim / lightly edited):
- "When we turned on bigger batches to save costs, some inference calls spiked in tail latency and we couldn't tell which model variant was the cause." (SaaS search product, mid-market)
- "We want clear guidance: which quant level is safe for document summarization vs. code completion?" (developer tooling startup)
- "Our accounting shows substantial token cost variance across routes — can the platform help us bundle similar routes under a single config?" (enterprise platform team)

Observed telemetry patterns that informed synthesis:
- Several customers show clustered cost improvements after enabling batching, but a subset saw 95th-percentile latency regressions correlated with heterogenous sequence lengths in the queue.
- Cache-hit ratios vary widely by workload; median per-customer prefix reuse is ~12% but top quartile hits approach 40%.
- Quantization regressions reported mainly on high-precision numeric extraction tasks (financial extraction, structured parsing).

Actionable buckets (prioritized):
1) "Batching Advisor" (Priority: P0 - pick first probe)
   - Problem: customers lack clear, safe defaults and visibility into batching tradeoffs across heterogeneous routes.
   - Proposed deliverable (MVP): API + Console suggestion card that, given a route's recent request distribution (seq len, tokens per request, QPS), recommends a conservative batch window and predicted latency/cost delta. Also include a toggle for "opt-in simulation" to run eco-simulated cost estimate before applying.
   - Success metrics: adoption by 10 pilot customers, average cost reduction >= 8% for opted routes, no increase in 95p latency above configured SLO for pilot group.
   - Ownership: product-optimize (Priya) + runtime (Marco) + console (Aisha).
   - Quick probe plan (2 weeks): build heuristic using existing request histograms, expose via internal API to 3 customers; collect telemetry.

2) "Cache Visibility and Conservative Prewarm" (Priority: P1)
   - Problem: cache behavior is opaque; customers can't attribute savings or diagnose missed reuse. Additionally, cold-starts for rarely seen prefixes cause expensive tokens.
   - Proposed deliverable (MVP): dashboard tile showing route-level cache-hit ratio, top prefixes by frequency, and estimated cost savings. Add a conservative prewarm action that can be scheduled per route (low-frequency synthetic prefetch) with guardrails to avoid pollution.
   - Success metrics: increase in median cache-hit ratio for pilot routes by 5–10%, and demonstrable cost reduction for routes with >15% prefix reuse.
   - Ownership: product-optimize (Aisha) + serving-runtime (Marco) + observability (SRE lead TBD).
   - Quick probe plan (3 weeks): surface existing cache counters in Console, run prewarm on 5 pilot routes, measure side effects.

3) "Quantization Playbook + Two Small Live Probes" (Priority: P1)
   - Problem: customers are uncertain which quant profiles are safe for their workloads; we see quality regressions in sensitive parsing tasks.
   - Proposed deliverable (MVP): a short playbook mapping common workload archetypes (summarization, code gen, extraction, classification) to recommended quant levels and what to expect. Run two controlled live probes: one for "safe lossy quant" on summarization routes, one for "conservative quant" on extraction routes.
   - Success metrics: documented quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metric) under acceptable thresholds for pilot customers; adoption intent from at least 3 teams.
   - Ownership: applied-ml (modeling lead) + product-optimize (Priya).
   - Quick probe plan (4 weeks): collect prompt-sets from 4 customers, run off-line evals vs. on-hosted inference, then run live AB for low-traffic windows.

Implementation risks and tradeoffs:
- Batch advisor miscues: heuristics could recommend batching that increases tail latency for workloads with large variance. Mitigation: conservative defaults + simulation and forced opt-in for first 30 days.
- Cache prewarm pollution: prefetch could evict more valuable cache entries. Mitigation: limit prewarm to routes with >20% repeated prefixes and cap prewarm QPS.
- Quantization regressions: some extraction tasks degrade non-linearly. Mitigation: require model-level fallback and automatic quality checks before rollout.

Open questions to resolve quickly:
- What level of console instrumentation is already accessible to the product-optimize team vs. needs infra changes? (action: Marco to map existing metrics by 2025-02-21)
- Can we simulate batching cost/latency on a dry-run path that mirrors production scheduling? (action: runtime team to prototype a simulator snippet)
- What privacy guardrails for collecting representative prompts from customers for playbook evals? (action: solutions eng to draft minimal-exposure prompt collection template)

Short-term roadmap (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: Align on pilot customers (3 for batching, 5 for cache prewarm, 4 for quant probes). Owners to confirm.
- Week 1–3: Launch batching advisor heuristic and internal API. Collect telemetry and iterate.
- Week 3–5: Expose cache metrics in Console and run conservative prewarm for pilot routes.
- Week 4–6: Run quant playbook offline evaluations; prepare AB rollout plan and quality checks.

Suggested pilot customers (rationale):
- SearchSaaS (mid-market): varied seq lengths, interested in cost savings; good telemetry.
- FinParse (enterprise): sensitive extraction work — target for conservative quant probe.
- NotesFlow (startup): high prefix reuse in chat session flows — good candidate for cache prewarm.

Appendix: quick heuristics notes (for runtime engineers)
- Batch window heuristic: recommended_batch_ms = clamp( median_latency_per_token * median_seq_len * 0.6, min=10ms, max=200ms ) adjusted upward for heavy QPS routes to avoid queue buildup.
- Cache prewarm policy: eligible if prefix_repeat_rate > 0.15 AND median_request_interval > 60s; prewarm QPS = min(0.1 * observed_peak_qps, 2 req/s).
- Quant check quick metric: for structured extraction, require strict-field-f1 >= baseline_f1 - 0.02 on validation prompts before allowing a quant profile to be recommended.

Next steps / asks for reviewers:
- Review and flag technical feasibility concerns (Marco) by 2025-02-24.
- Product: confirm pilot customer list and outreach plan (Priya) by 2025-02-25.
- Solutions eng: draft prompt collection template and privacy guardrail checklist by 2025-02-28.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally concise — once owners sign off, I'll expand into a Confluence playbook with implementation checklists and a JIRA epic structure.

Document history:
- 2025-02-18: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-21: added telemetry excerpts and quick heuristics (Marco)
- 2025-03-03: updated ownership and pilot list after sync (Aisha)
